details: Global crypto markets experienced $114 million in liquidations over the past 24 hours, with long positions accounting for $63.09 million. This occurred during a broad "risk-off" phase, influenced by spiking US Treasury yields and sustained high oil prices, which contribute to inflation worries and a hawkish central bank stance. Major altcoins bore the brunt of over $425-$500 million in leveraged long position liquidations.
title: Crypto Market Sees $114M Liquidations Amid Risk-Off Sentiment

details: The European System of Central Banks (ESCB) has recommended that stablecoin issuers should not be required to hold a minimum proportion of their reserves as bank deposits. Citing potential "run risk" exposure to banks, the ESCB suggests that reserves instead be held in assets maturing within one to five working days. This recommendation comes in response to the EU's Markets in Crypto Assets (MiCA) regulations.
title: EU Central Banks Urge Stablecoin Reserve Policy Shift

details: The US Federal Reserve has introduced two proposals under the GENIUS Act aimed at regulating payment stablecoins. A key proposal mandates that Fed-supervised stablecoin issuers fully back their coins with high-quality liquid assets, such as short-term Treasuries, and establishes standardized capital requirements. These rules also aim to clarify permissible stablecoin activities for banks under Fed supervision.
title: US Fed Proposes Strict Stablecoin Backing Requirements

details: Recent reports highlight cryptocurrency's central and growing role in helping Iran circumvent international sanctions, particularly concerning war financing. Similar methods are reportedly being used for Russian sanctions workarounds, with a Moscow-based financial firm, A7, utilizing a ruble-pegged cryptocurrency for evasion since early 2025.
title: Crypto Continues to Aid Iranian Sanctions Evasion
